summary: In this excerpt from the novel Little Brother (Book 1, part 17), the narrator, Marcus, and his friends Darryl, Van and Jolu are stranded after a terrorist attack on San Francisco disables phones and the internet. Darryl is badly wounded, and the group tries to flag down emergency vehicles on Market Street, but ambulances, cop cars and fire engines drive past. The narrator finally steps into the road and stops a car that turns out to be an unmarked military-looking Jeep, whose occupants wear coveralls, carry rifles and hooded gas masks.
one_line: Injured Darryl and his friends try to flag down help on Market Street after a terrorist attack, only to be confronted by armed, masked men in an unmarked Jeep.
key_facts: The narrator says he was no longer thinking of helping anyone and was focused on finding spaces to move into and holding onto Darryl and Van.
Jolu asked the narrator to call 911, and the call produced a whimper-like sound rather than a busy signal.
The narrator says the 911 failure is like what happens when three million people dial the same number at once.
Darryl pointed out the cop cars, ambulances and firetrucks passing on the street as possible sources of help.
Darryl dragged himself down toward Market Street, white-faced and panting, while Van's sweater was soaked in blood.
An ambulance, a cop car, a firetruck and the next three cop cars all drove past without slowing down.
The narrator stepped into the road waving his arms and shouting "STOP" at an approaching car.
The stopped vehicle was a military-looking Jeep, like an armored Hummer, with no military insignia.
The narrator jumped back, lost his balance and ended up on the road when the Jeep skidded to a stop in front of him.
The occupants wore coveralls, carried big bulky rifles and had hooded gas masks with tinted face-plates.
Darryl insisted he was fine and that they should let him up, while Van told him to shut up and lie still.
The narrator says that the terrorists could be blamed for the lack of phone and data service.
